opsonized-zymosan inhibiting cytoplasmic motion of AM is mediated by an external calcium influx.

the mechanism of changes in the activities of alveolar phagocytes induced by phagocytosis.
the mechanisms of changes of cytoplasmic motion of alveolar cells caused by phagocyte stimulus.
the effects of phagocytosis on AM activities.

OZ inhibits cytoplamic motility of AM in vitro, and the mechanism of OZ-induced effects may be due to the influx of calcium into AM.
the phagocytic process of AM may inhibit cytoplasmic movements of AM, which are related to the cytoplasmic contractile apparatus, via external calcium influx.

phagocytosis by AM is associated with a decrease of cytoplasmic motion, and the inhibition of the cytoplasmic movement of AM is due to the increase in intracellular concentration of calcium.

opsonized phagocytic stimuli inhibit cytoplasmic motion of AM by increasing external calcium influx.
